newsitem.title: USA: USDA economist - U.S. corn crop near 9 bln bushels.
newsitem.headline: USDA economist - U.S. corn crop near 9 bln bushels.

text.p: The U.S. corn crop "will be near nine billion bushels," Keith Collins, chief economist at the Agriculture Department said Wednesday.
His comments suggested a harvest somewhat larger than the 8.8 billion bushels forecast by USDA last month.
Collins said favorable weather and the increased maturity of the crop indicated the harvest would be larger.
"I would think that we're looking at a pretty good crop this year," Collins told reporters after testifying to the Senate Agriculture Committee.
A cold, rainy spring delayed corn plantings, but Collins noted there have been no hard frosts yet and that weather forecasts indicated mild weather in the near future.
During his testimony, Collins told lawmakers the U.S. corn crop "will be near nine billion bushels."
